Blains
BLAYNZ
noun
From Old English blegen, a blister, pustule, or inflamed swelling. The Hebrew is ’aba’bu’oth, blistering eruptions. The word names the pustules of the sixth plague, the boil breaking forth with blains upon man and beast.

Biblical Definition

Blains are blisters or angry pustules that break out upon the skin, the fruit of the sixth plague of Egypt. Moses was commanded to take ashes of the furnace and sprinkle them toward heaven, and it shall become small dust in all the land of Egypt, and shall be a boil breaking forth with blains upon man, and upon beast, throughout all the land of Egypt (Exo 9:9). So it came to pass: Moses sprinkled it up toward heaven; and it became a boil breaking forth with blains upon man, and upon beast (Exo 9:10). This plague marks a solemn escalation—the earlier judgments fell on the river, the land, the cattle, but now the stroke lands on the bodies of the Egyptians themselves, and upon the magicians first of all, who could not stand before Moses because of the boils (Exo 9:11). The ashes of the furnace are a fit emblem: Egypt’s furnaces, in which Israel had been made to labor and to suffer, now became the seed of Egypt’s torment, the LORD turning the instruments of oppression into the means of judgment. The boil with its blains is one of the very curses threatened against a disobedient Israel, the botch of Egypt... and with the itch, whereof thou canst not be healed (Deu 28:27), and a sore botch that cannot be healed (Deu 28:35). Blains thus preach that the God who afflicts the proud oppressor with running sores will as surely afflict His own people if they walk in Egypt’s hardness; the plague is a mercy that warns before it wounds.

Webster 1828 Definition

A blister, pustule, or inflamed swelling breaking out upon the skin.

expand to see more

BLAIN, n. [Old Eng. blegen, a blister or pustule.] A pustule; a botch; a blister; a rising or swelling upon the skin, filled with matter and inflamed.

In Scripture, the eruptions of the sixth plague of Egypt, a boil breaking forth with blains upon man and beast (Exod. ix. 9, 10).

The plural, blains, denotes the angry pustules that accompany a boil or botch.

One of the sores threatened in the curses of the covenant against a disobedient people (Deut. xxviii.).

Figuratively, an outward eruption bearing witness to an inward corruption, the sickness of the flesh answering to the sin of the heart.

Key Scripture

Exo 9:9 — "And it shall become small dust in all the land of Egypt, and shall be a boil breaking forth with blains upon man, and upon beast, throughout all the land of Egypt."

Exo 9:10 — "And they took ashes of the furnace, and stood before Pharaoh; and Moses sprinkled it up toward heaven; and it became a boil breaking forth with blains upon man, and upon beast."

Deu 28:27 — "The LORD will smite thee with the botch of Egypt, and with the emerods , and with the scab, and with the itch, whereof thou canst not be healed."

Deu 28:35 — "The LORD shall smite thee in the knees, and in the legs, with a sore botch that cannot be healed, from the sole of thy foot unto the top of thy head."

Modern Corruption

Not a contested doctrine but a plague upon the flesh; it recovers the truth that outward affliction can be the just recompense of inward hardness.

expand to see more

The present age likes its judgments impersonal—a disease is a mechanism, never a message, and to read a moral meaning in a pox is thought a relic of darker times. Yet the blains fell by the deliberate act of Moses, from the ashes of the very furnaces where Israel had groaned, and they fell first upon the magicians who had aped the works of God. The plague was legible: it turned the oppressor’s own instrument of cruelty into the seed of his torment, and it struck the counterfeiters of miracles so that they could not so much as stand. Where men harden themselves against plain warnings, the warnings sometimes take up residence in the body.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the same boil which fell on Egypt is named among the curses that would fall on Israel herself—that God is no respecter of persons, and the sin He punishes in Pharaoh He will not excuse in His own if they walk in Pharaoh’s hardness. The blains are a mercy in the form of a wound, warning the flesh of a judgment the heart may still flee.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

A word for skin-pustules rooted in the Old English for a blister.

expand to see more

Old English blegen—a blister, pustule, or inflamed swelling of the skin.

Hebrew ’aba’bu’oth—blistering eruptions, the pustules that break forth from a boil.

Paired always with “boil” in the KJV: a boil breaking forth with blains, the sixth plague of Egypt.

Born of the ashes of the furnace—the instrument of Israel’s oppression turned into the seed of Egypt’s torment.

Kin to the botch and the scab of Deuteronomy 28, the incurable sores of the covenant curse.

Usage

"The magicians who counterfeited the plagues could not stand for the blains that were upon them."

"From the ashes of Israel’s furnaces came the blains that tormented Israel’s taskmasters."

"The blains upon the skin were a legible judgment, the body made to publish the sin of the heart."
